posts.title: Off-Menu video editing: the agent writes the functions the editor lacks
posts.description: OpenScreen 2.1 introduces Off-Menu. The built-in functions stay; next to them, a low-level layer where a coding agent writes the function the editor lacks, through MCP and inside guardrails. Visual effects come first. What it took, what it costs, and who got close before.

posts.title: Making of v2: a demo is never ugly
posts.description: How OpenScreen v2 came together. One rule, an audit against it, twenty-one pull requests merged into one branch, and a round of UI work that removed more than it added.

posts.title: An export benchmark built to be hard to fake
posts.description: An open, reproducible screen recorder export benchmark. Same clip, same edit, each result divided by ffmpeg on the same machine and verified in pixels.
